The Kiro CLI

Usage: kiro-cli [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  agent         Manage agents
  chat          AI assistant in your terminal
  login         Log in to Kiro
  logout        Log out of Kiro
  whoami        Print info about the current login session
  profile       Show the profile associated with this idc user
  settings      Customize appearance & behavior
  diagnostic    Run diagnostic tests
  issue         Create a new Github issue
  crew          Launch Kiro Crew, installing it if it is not already installed
  mcp           Model Context Protocol (MCP)
  powers        Manage Powers (install and uninstall plugins)
  update        Check for and install updates
  integrations  Manage system integrations
  serve         Start a persistent WebSocket server for the v3 engine
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -v, --verbose...              Increase logging verbosity
      --agent <AGENT>           Launch chat with the given agent, shorthand for chat --agent
      --tui                     Launch chat in TUI mode
      --legacy-ui               Launch chat in legacy UI mode [aliases: --classic]
      --v3                      Launch the next generation Kiro agent
      --v2                      Use the V2 agent engine (the pre-3.0 default)
  -r, --resume                  Resume the most recent conversation from this directory
      --resume-id <SESSION_ID>  Resume a specific conversation by session ID
      --resume-picker           Interactively select a conversation to resume from this directory
                                [aliases: --list]
      --cloud                   Run this session in a cloud sandbox, shorthand for chat --cloud
      --repo <REPO>             Repository to open in a cloud session, shorthand for chat --repo
  -h, --help                    Print help
  -V, --version                 Print version

AI assistant in your terminal

Usage: kiro-cli chat [OPTIONS] [INPUT]

Arguments:
  [INPUT]
          The first question to ask

Options:
  -r, --resume
          Resume the most recent conversation from this directory

      --resume-id <SESSION_ID>
          Resume a specific conversation by session ID

      --resume-picker
          Interactively select a conversation to resume from this directory

      --sessions
          Launch straight into the session dashboard (V3/KAS only); closing it exits rather than
          dropping into a chat

      --agent <AGENT>
          Context profile to use

      --model <MODEL>
          Current model to use

      --effort <EFFORT>
          Initial effort level (e.g. low, medium, high, xhigh, max)

  -a, --trust-all-tools
          Allows the model to use any tool to run commands without asking for confirmation

      --trust-tools <TOOL_NAMES>
          Trust only this set of tools. Example: trust some tools: '--trust-tools=fs_read,fs_write',
          trust no tools: '--trust-tools='

      --no-interactive
          Whether the command should run without expecting user input

      --trust-workspace
          Skip the "Trust this workspace?" prompt for this launch only (V3 only). Hooks, agents, MCP
          servers and workflows from this folder load without asking; the decision is not saved, so
          a folder that is not already trusted asks again next launch

  -l, --list-sessions
          List all saved chat sessions for the current directory

      --all-cwds
          With --list-sessions: span every workspace (local stores only), emitting one envelope per
          cwd in JSON output

      --list-models
          List available models and exit

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format for list commands (used with --list-models and --list-sessions)

          Possible values:
          - plain:       Outputs the results as markdown
          - json:        Outputs the results as JSON
          - json-pretty: Outputs the results as pretty print JSON
          
          [default: plain]

      --output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>
          Response stream format: text (default), or stream-json for JSON Lines on stdout. 
          stream-json implies --no-interactive

          Possible values:
          - text:        Human-readable text
          - stream-json: The run's ACP events as JSON Lines on stdout, one self-describing event per
            line
          
          [default: text]

  -d, --delete-session <SESSION_ID>
          Delete a saved chat session by ID

      --session-source <v1|v2>
          Target only v1 or v2 store for --delete-session (default: both)
          
          [possible values: v1, v2]

  -w, --wrap <WRAP>
          Control line wrapping behavior (default: auto-detect)

          Possible values:
          - always: Always wrap at terminal width
          - never:  Never wrap (raw output)
          - auto:   Auto-detect based on output target (default)

      --require-mcp-startup
          Require all enabled MCP servers to start successfully; exit with code 3 if any fail

      --tui
          Use the new terminal UI

      --legacy-ui
          Use the legacy harness
          
          [aliases: --classic]

      --agent-engine <ENGINE>
          Agent engine to use: "v1", "v2" (default), or "v3"
          
          [possible values: v2, v1, v3]

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase logging verbosity

      --v3
          Launch the next generation Kiro agent

      --v2
          Use the V2 agent engine (the pre-3.0 default)

      --mode <MODE>
          Mode to use with the V3 agent: "default" or "spec"
          
          [possible values: default, spec]

      --cloud
          Run this session in a cloud sandbox (V3/KAS only), interactively or with --no-interactive.
          Sends _meta.kiro.executionTarget on session/new

      --repo <REPO>
          Repository to open in a cloud session, as name or owner/name (comma-separated for
          multiple). Only meaningful with --cloud

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Internal subcommands. Surface for tests and TUI IPC. May break without notice. Not for direct
end-user use

Usage: kiro-cli chat _ [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  windows-sandbox            
  export-session             Export a session to a portable zip archive
  import-session             Import a session from a portable zip archive
  get-kas-token              Resolve and refresh-if-expired the active OIDC access token for KAS.
                             Wire surface for the _kiro/auth/getAccessToken ACP extension
  get-telemetry-credentials  Resolve the bearer credential the TUI telemetry exporter signs KUTS
                             batches with, bound to the stored token's lineage. Wire surface for 
                             @kiro/tui-telemetry/meter.ts
  ensure-session             Convert a session between V2 and KAS formats if needed, and ensure it
                             is loadable in the target engine
  derive-messages            Derive the V2 model-context messages from a V2 session log. Used as the
                             "expected" side in cross-engine converter tests
  test-seed-v1               Seed a V1 conversation row into a sandbox SQLite from a fixture JSON
                             file. Refuses to run unless KIRO_TEST_DB_PATH is set
  upgrade-agent              Scan or run the agent-config universal-format migration. Wire surface
                             for the /upgrade-agent TUI panels
  refresh-feed               Fetch the remote changelog feed (bounded blocking fetch) and snapshot
                             it to the feed file the TUI reads. Wire surface for the /changelog
                             panel's fresh-on-request refresh
  midway-expiry              Print the current Midway session expiry for the status-line segment.
                             Wire surface for the TUI's live-refresh (mtime-triggered) poll
  help                       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -v, --verbose...  Increase logging verbosity
  -h, --help        Print help

Resolve and refresh-if-expired the active OIDC access token for KAS. Wire surface for the 
_kiro/auth/getAccessToken ACP extension

Usage: kiro-cli chat _ get-kas-token [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --reason <REASON>
          Why KAS asked for a fresh token (informational; logged only)
      --current-expires-at <CURRENT_EXPIRES_AT>
          ISO-8601 expiry of KAS's currently-cached token (informational)
      --force-refresh
          Force a network token refresh even when the cached token looks valid. Set by the TUI host
          handler when KAS sends forceRefresh on the getAccessToken covenant during mid-turn 401
          recovery
  -v, --verbose...
          Increase logging verbosity
  -h, --help
          Print help

Start Agent Client Protocol (ACP) agent

Usage: kiro-cli acp [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --agent <AGENT>
          Name of the agent to use when starting the first session

      --model <MODEL>
          Model ID to use when starting the first session

      --effort <EFFORT>
          Initial effort level (e.g. low, medium, high, xhigh, max)

  -a, --trust-all-tools
          Auto-approve all tool permission requests

      --trust-tools <TOOL_NAMES>
          Trust only this set of tools

      --agent-engine <ENGINE>
          Agent engine to use: "v1", "v2", or "v3". Overrides the acp.agentEngine setting; v2 when
          neither is set
          
          [possible values: v2, v1, v3]

      --auth-method <METHOD>
          Authentication owner for the v3 engine. Defaults to "cli", which uses the kiro-cli login
          session; use "client" to answer the engine's access-token requests from the ACP client

          Possible values:
          - cli:    Resolve access tokens for the v3 engine from the Kiro CLI credential store
            (default)
          - client: Forward the v3 engine's access-token requests to the ACP client
          
          [aliases: --authMethod]

      --login
          Log in interactively and exit, for ACP clients that run terminal authentication

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase logging verbosity

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Customize appearance & behavior

Usage: kiro-cli settings [OPTIONS] [KEY] [VALUE]
       kiro-cli settings <COMMAND>

Commands:
  open  Open the settings file
  list  List settings
  help  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Arguments:
  [KEY]
          key

  [VALUE]
          value

Options:
  -d, --delete
          Delete a key (No value needed)

      --global
          Set or delete in global settings (default)

      --workspace
          Set or delete in workspace settings

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Format of the output

          Possible values:
          - plain:       Outputs the results as markdown
          - json:        Outputs the results as JSON
          - json-pretty: Outputs the results as pretty print JSON
          
          [default: plain]

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase logging verbosity

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Manage agents

Usage: kiro-cli agent [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  list         List the available agents. Note that local agents are only discovered if the command
               is invoked at a directory that contains them
  create       Create an agent config. If path is not provided, Kiro CLI shall create this config in
               the global agent directory
  edit         Edit an existing agent config
  validate     Validate a config with the given path
  migrate      Migrate profiles to agent Note that doing this is potentially destructive to agents
               that are already in the global agent directories
  upgrade      Upgrade agent configs in a directory to the universal format both engines load.
               Rewrites top-level *.json files in place (subdirectories are not searched);
               already-universal, V3-only, out-of-sync, and externally managed agents are left
               untouched
  set-default  Define a default agent to use when kiro-cli chat launches
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -v, --verbose...  Increase logging verbosity
  -h, --help        Print help
